rejected.idea_brief: Hard-coded customer/ID sweeps — iterating over hard-coded customer or ID lists instead of the DB-enabled records.
rejected.cause: THE PROCESS-ALL-ENABLED LAW (banked Sept 17, user-corrected): cron jobs / alerts / scripts iterate over the DB (enabled customers, active records), never hard-coded IDs — scales without code edits.

rejected.idea_brief: Customer-facing rebates attached to deal alerts or purchases.
rejected.cause: MPA program terms 4.2d bar customer-facing rebates — banked with the affiliate doctrine (EPN qualifying-links, Oct 17): deal alerts are qualifying links by design; no rebate layer on top.

rejected.idea_brief: Publishing the forward-chain / engine names (public label for the internal engine-grade pipeline).
rejected.cause: THE NAMING LAW: pull-query/forward-chain and engine names stay private (banked Oct 20 pull-query naming law; the Nov-11 Camel execution-spec flags ENGINE-GRADE rename as founder-decision — the engine names are never published in public copy).

rejected.idea_brief: The falsify-word civic-language framing (claim dressing/labeling that fails reproducibility).
rejected.cause: THE REPRODUCIBILITY-LAW SUPERSEDES: every claim verified, all in git, all reproducible — the falsify-word civic-language pattern is vetoed wherever it conflicts. (Banked in the working-notes reproducibility standard.)

rejected.idea_brief: Mixing graded and ungraded rows into one raw-median computation.
rejected.cause: GRADED-ROWS-SEPARATE LAW: graded and ungraded rows stay separate in any median/summary math — caught the same day it was tried (banked with the Oct-13 study-arm traps).

rejected.idea_brief: Naive ask-times-N corner math (multiplying observed ask prices by N to estimate volume/value).
rejected.cause: THE SUPPLY-LADDER LAW (transplanted Oct 14, ~230-row NBA probe): value sits on a 6.3x-100x supply ladder with rung multipliers — naive linear ask-times-N multiplication at the corners is structurally wrong.

rejected.idea_brief: Bypass edits to memory files (patch/shell writes around the memory-tool guard).
rejected.cause: THE TOOL-CLEAN LAW + MEMORY-TOOL GUARD #26045 (Nov-6): MEMORY.md and memory files are edited only through their owning tools — shell/patch bypass edits get rejected ('file wouldn't round-trip') and are vetoed as a class.

rejected.idea_brief: Classifying bookings as reactive (the reactive-bookings classification claim).
rejected.cause: THE NIGHT'S RETRACTION — the reactive-bookings-classification claim was withdrawn by the verifier; re-test only after the facility grain widens (banked in the multi-state within-state panel working notes).

rejected.idea_brief: Apify-actor-class volume scrapes as the standing collection route.
rejected.cause: THE SCALE-COST LAW: Apify per-run costs (~$0.04-0.05/card/run, banked Sept 14; Starter $29/mo) lose at scale to BrightData-class routes (BD free 5K/mo, web_unlocker1) — volume scraping goes BD/BrightData-class, not Apify-actor-class.

rejected.idea_brief: Oversized-commit pattern — committing giant source files (>100MB PDFs) whole to the repo.
rejected.cause: THE SPLIT-AND-TAG-LAW INSTEAD (Nov-22, founder-trick): critical source-PDF > GitHub's 100MB cap = split into <=90MB blocks + reassembly manifest (SHA256 per block + source-hash, byte-counts). Session-proven: the 118MB MO budget PDF in a committed cache dir silently hard-failed the push.
